title: Estimation and orders of magnitude; Scalars and vectors
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MS05-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MS05-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MS05-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MS04-1#N.3, MS05-1#N.4, MS04-1#N.6, MS05-1#N.13, MS04-1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Order of magnitude
items.clue: The nearest power of ten to a value.

items.label: Scalar
items.clue: Quantity with magnitude only, such as speed, mass or energy.

items.label: Vector
items.clue: Quantity with magnitude and direction, such as force or momentum.

items.label: Components
items.clue: Two perpendicular parts that together replace the original arrow.

questions.stem: Kinetic energy = ½ × mass × speed². What is the order of magnitude of the kinetic energy of an adult walking?
questions.explanation: ½ × 70 kg × (1.5 m s⁻¹)² ≈ 80 J, nearest power of ten 10² J.

questions.stem: A hiker walks 5 m east and then 9 m west along a straight path. Student 1 takes east as the positive direction; Student 2 takes west as the positive direction. Each finds the hiker's resultant displacement as a signed component. Which statement correctly compares their results?

options.text: Only Student 1 can be right, as east has to be the positive direction.
Student 1 gets −4 m and Student 2 gets +4 m, and both results mean 4 m west.
Both get +4 m, by subtracting the smaller distance from the larger.
Both get 14 m, since the two walks simply add to give the resultant.

questions.stem: What is the best estimate of the volume of water in a full bath?
questions.explanation: About 1.5 m × 0.6 m × 0.4 m ≈ 0.4 m³ (about 400 litres).

questions.stem: A robot vacuum moves 1.1 m east and then 1.6 m north, each along a straight line. What is the magnitude of its displacement from its starting point?
A classroom is about 8 m long, 6 m wide and 3 m high. What is the order of magnitude of the mass of air in it?
questions.explanation: Volume ≈ 8 × 6 × 3 = 144 m³. Mass ≈ 144 × 1.2 ≈ 170 kg, order 10² kg.
